content: Indication-specific dosing for slippery elm includes the following regimens: Oral administration of 4-16 mL three times daily (TID). Oral administration of 4 grams of slippery elm mixed in 500 mL of water, taken three times daily (TID). Oral administration of 5 mL three times daily (TID) in a 1:1 solution with 60% alcohol. For topical application, mix powdered inner bark with boiling water and apply to the affected area. Slippery elm is used for a variety of conditions, including colitis, diverticulitis, constipation, cough, cystitis, diarrhea, irritable bowel syndrome, skin wounds or inflammation (topical use), sore throat, ulcer prevention, and urinary tract infections. It is also applied for wounds, burns, gout, rheumatism, cold sores, boils, abscesses, ulcers, toothaches, sore throat, and as a lubricant to ease labor. The effectiveness of slippery elm is well-documented for sore throat relief, but evidence for its efficacy in other conditions remains inconclusive. Adverse effects include allergic reactions, contact dermatitis, and hypersensitivity to pollen. The whole bark of slippery elm is considered an abortifacient and should not be used during pregnancy. Pregnancy considerations: Slippery elm is classified as an abortifacient when the whole bark is used. It is advised to avoid use during lactation. Pregnancy Category A: Generally acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Pharmacokinetics: Metabolism: Not available (N/A). Excretion: Not available (N/A). The mucilage derived from the inner bark is the primary active component responsible for its therapeutic effects.
